automountServiceAccountToken.description:
Mount the ServiceAccount API token into the pod.
Set on the pod itself, which is what actually keeps the token out of the container: the
ServiceAccount-level setting is ignored as soon as a pod names a different account.
automountServiceAccountToken.title: automountServiceAccountToken

commonAnnotations.description: Annotations added to every object the chart creates. Values may contain Go templates.
commonAnnotations.title: commonAnnotations

commonLabels.description: Labels added to every object the chart creates. Values may contain Go templates.
commonLabels.title: commonLabels

extraEnv.description: Additional environment variables appended to the application container.
extraEnv.title: extraEnv

extraVolumeMounts.description: Additional volume mounts added to the application container.
extraVolumeMounts.title: extraVolumeMounts

extraVolumes.description: Additional volumes added to the pod.
extraVolumes.title: extraVolumes

fullnameOverride.description: Override the full generated resource name.
fullnameOverride.title: fullnameOverride

global.description: Global values are values that can be accessed from any chart or subchart by exactly the same name.
global.title: global

hostAliases.description: Host aliases injected into the pod's /etc/hosts.
hostAliases.title: hostAliases

digest.description:
Image digest (`sha256:...`). Combined with `tag` rather than replacing it: the digest
pins the pull, while `tag` stays on as the readable version marker.
digest.title: digest

pullPolicy.description:
Image pull policy. Left empty, resolves to `Always` for the `latest` tag and
`IfNotPresent` for anything pinned.
pullPolicy.title: pullPolicy

registry.description: Registry host. Left empty, the repository is used as-is (Docker Hub).
registry.title: registry

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart's `appVersion`.
tag.title: tag

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull secrets for private registries. Accepts `- name: regcred` or the shorthand `- regcred`.
imagePullSecrets.title: imagePullSecrets

kubeVersionOverride.description:
Kubernetes version to target when branching on API availability.
Lets `helm template` render for a specific cluster version without a live connection.
Leave empty to detect from the cluster.
kubeVersionOverride.title: kubeVersionOverride

livenessProbe.description: Liveness probe. See `startupProbe` for the accepted shape.
livenessProbe.title: livenessProbe

nameOverride.description: Override the chart name used in resource names and labels.
nameOverride.title: nameOverride

namespaceOverride.description: Deploy into a namespace other than the release namespace.
namespaceOverride.title: namespaceOverride

networkPolicy.description:
Network policy configuration.

Every generated egress rule is scoped by a `to:` selector. An egress rule that lists only
ports is not a restriction — the NetworkPolicy API reads a missing `to` as "any
destination", so such a policy permits traffic to every in-cluster service and to the
cloud metadata endpoint.

cidr.description: Destination CIDR for the HTTP/HTTPS rules.
cidr.title: cidr

customRules.description: Additional egress rules, appended verbatim. Each must carry its own `to:` selector.
customRules.title: customRules

enabled.description: Allow egress to the cluster DNS service.
enabled.title: enabled

namespaceSelector.description: Namespace selector for the DNS service.
namespaceSelector.title: namespaceSelector

podSelector.description: Pod selector for the DNS service.
podSelector.title: podSelector

enabled.description: Add egress rules. Disabled means default-deny for outbound traffic.
enabled.title: enabled

except.description:
CIDRs carved out of `cidr`. Defaults exclude RFC1918 private space and link-local
169.254.0.0/16, which covers the cloud instance metadata endpoint.
except.title: except

enabled.description: Allow egress to TCP/80 on the destinations described by `cidr`/`except`.
enabled.title: enabled

enabled.description: Allow egress to TCP/443 on the destinations described by `cidr`/`except`.
enabled.title: enabled

enabled.description:
Create the NetworkPolicies. When enabled with no rules configured, the result is a
default-deny policy, which is intentional.
enabled.title: enabled

extraEgress.description: Extra egress rules appended regardless of `egress.enabled`.
extraEgress.title: extraEgress

extraIngress.description: Extra ingress rules appended regardless of `ingress.enabled`.
extraIngress.title: extraIngress

controller.description: Allow traffic from the ingress controller.

enabled.description: Allow ingress from the ingress controller.
enabled.title: enabled

namespace.description: Namespace the ingress controller runs in.
namespace.title: namespace

ports.description: Restrict the rule to specific ports. Empty means all ports.
ports.title: ports

selector.description: Pod selector matching the ingress controller.
selector.title: selector

controller.title: controller

enabled.description: Add ingress rules. Disabled means default-deny for inbound traffic.
enabled.title: enabled

monitoring.description: Allow scraping from a monitoring namespace.

enabled.description: Allow ingress from the monitoring namespace.
enabled.title: enabled

ports.description: Restrict the rule to specific ports. Empty means all ports.
ports.title: ports

monitoring.title: monitoring

networkPolicy.title: networkPolicy

podAnnotations.description: Annotations added to the pod template.
podAnnotations.title: podAnnotations

podAntiAffinity.description: Shorthand for spreading replicas across nodes. `soft` prefers, `hard` requires.
podAntiAffinity.title: podAntiAffinity

podLabels.description: Labels added to the pod template.
podLabels.title: podLabels

podSecurityContextPreset.description:
Baseline for the pod security context. `restricted` applies the Pod Security Standards
restricted profile (`runAsNonRoot`, `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault`,
`fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`); `none` applies nothing. Identity fields
(`runAsUser`, `runAsGroup`, `fsGroup`) are always left to the chart, since they must match
the UID baked into the image.
podSecurityContextPreset.title: podSecurityContextPreset

readinessProbe.description: Readiness probe. See `startupProbe` for the accepted shape.
readinessProbe.title: readinessProbe

resourcesPreset.description:
Named resource sizing. Ignored when `resources` is set.
Presets set a memory limit and CPU/memory requests but no CPU limit: a CPU limit does not
protect the node the way a memory limit does, it only throttles this workload.
resourcesPreset.title: resourcesPreset

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Number of old ReplicaSets to retain for rollback.
revisionHistoryLimit.title: revisionHistoryLimit

securityContextPreset.description:
Baseline for the container security context. `restricted` drops all capabilities and
forbids privilege escalation, a writable root filesystem and running as root.
securityContextPreset.title: securityContextPreset

automountToken.description: Mount the API token into pods that default to this ServiceAccount.
automountToken.title: automountToken

name.description: Name of the ServiceAccount. Generated when empty.
name.title: name

startupProbe.description:
Startup probe. Set `enabled` and exactly one handler (`httpGet`, `tcpSocket`, `exec`
or `grpc`); unset timing fields fall back to the Kubernetes defaults.
startupProbe.title: startupProbe
